trials.rationale: The clean objective is communication-wire-bound, so the only structural lever that preserves the frozen two-rank global batch, FP32 policy and quality is cutting per-step bytes on the wire. Measured evidence: baseline step_ms 176.15/176.20ms (ranks 0/1) with communication_without_compute_ms 126.2-127.6ms and communication_kernel_sum_ms 168-170ms; the separate nsys timeline capture (wall 200.4ms, kernel active union 175.7ms) shows 74 NCCL collectives per step whose kernels occupy 163.8ms: 48 block all-gathers of 25,192,448B at ~2.02ms each, 24 block reduce-scatters at ~2.09ms, the root-unit 105MB all-gather (8.23ms) and root 210MB-input reduce-scatter (8.20ms). NCCL tuning logs confirm RING/SIMPLE over 2 channels for both sizes, so these durations are bandwidth, not latency; device telemetry shows no NVLink (NVML status 3) with pcie.tx/rx sustained at 12-14.7GB/s, matching ~2.02GB moved per rank per step at ~12.5GB/s. NCCL algorithm/env retuning is not reachable because the worker initializes the process group before the adapter runs and the adapter must not create another one. The joint candidate replaces the model-boundary forward (group 6d8291a335bb2fbe9907, absorbing the GPT2Model driver 08b6c9c34034f5941d52) with a vocab-sharded head/embedding that respects the existing dim-0 shard layout: it computes lm_head and the token/position embeddings per shard (tied wte stays DTensor Shard(0); lm_head weight-grad and dh become shard GEMMs), exchanging only the peer hidden state (0.5MB), logits shards (12.9MB) and a backward dlogits slice (12.9MB) instead of the root unit's 105MB forward all-gather (e7538ec995b75a881584 plus its copy-in and split satellites 4fc3765bd87629cf5e19, 67e19c14af2c21ea38b5, 24eaa0b2763e423f279b) and 105MB backward reduce-scatter (e086fbcf542dab75ce4c plus its chunk_cat satellite fdcefa872a4767b9778f); the replaced embedding/lm_head bundles (16215834131465e9bc70, 8d571647f35364a31a96, 7dc4727d492d36f7db02, a4b9b811be2319bdc0ee, 877ffdb3cfbf063c6c90, d7c106bf7846541c7c89, 852c8b7031ad02e802b2, 7c8149e0170d5f5fd75f, 37e8bc8d9aabca710209, 051ac0bc11fac605e05d, 88c55222b0766cd5bf2b) and small helper ops inside the bypassed GPT2Model path are subsumed by that boundary. Cross-rank gradient combination reproduces the semantics verified in torch 2.13 _fsdp_collectives._get_gradient_divide_factors (FP32, DP size 2 -> ReduceOp.AVG): each shard grad is 0.5*(own-sequence + peer-sequence contribution), with the peer contribution computed locally from the exchanged dlogits slice and hidden state, so no full 205.9MB wte grad or 210MB reduce-scatter input buffer is ever materialized. The head edit needs its companion edit: the memory it frees (root all-gather output, unsharded root residency, full-grad buffer) funds calling FSDPModule.set_reshard_after_forward(False) (verified runtime API on the worker's torch 2.13.0+cu129) on the last K transformer blocks from within the replacement, removing K of the 48 block all-gathers in group 04dbf05d596cce5394b5 (K x 25.2MB, ~2.0ms each); keep-K alone is memory-infeasible since usable headroom over the 2239MB baseline peak is only ~112MB, and block reduce-scatter scheduling in b94714d9702670fe2605 is co-managed, with backward prefetch re-established via set_modules_to_backward_prefetch/unshard(async_op=True) because the bypassed root hook normally initiates it. Blocks keep their standard FSDP hooks and call coverage; loss, complete logits (assembled from the same GEMM pieces, reassociation error ~1e-7 vs atol 1e-6/rtol 1e-4), completion boundaries, memory sampling lifetime and the tied-embedding identity are unchanged.

Repair within the same boundary: perform every cross-rank exchange as a collective on the worker's existing default NCCL group (all_gather_into_tensor of the shard piece; at world_size 2 each rank sends exactly its own N bytes and receives the peer's N - wire-equivalent to the intended swap, no ordering discipline, no tags, no new process group, same RING/SIMPLE path FSDP itself uses), keep the verified-shard math (shard-local lm_head/embedding GEMMs, explicit 0.5*(own+peer) gradient combination reproducing FSDP's ReduceOp.AVG semantics, grads set in the actual DTensor shard layout, tied wte identity untouched, loss/logits/completion boundaries and memory-sampling lifetime unchanged), and land the first revision at keep_unsharded_blocks=0 so the transport repair is isolated before any block-reshard policy change; K>0 via FSDPModule.set_reshard_after_forward(False) (verified present in this torch) stays memory-gated by the 2351.2 MB (1.05x) peak constraint, affordable only because the head edit frees ~300+ MB of root transients (each kept block adds ~50.3 MB from forward to post-backward reshard). trials.rationale: Repair the previous family's concrete, now-measured failure on a smaller exact-numerics boundary. Previous trial-86e14487d0 (same model-forward joint boundary, 21 groups) did NOT hang: its collective-transport repair worked (all three parameter runs passed the worker, exit 0, coverage 2/2 invocations of b08a96298d855d7c8dcd7497, zero exception/false-return events), but it failed quality at continuous update 2 - logits max_abs_error 4.53e-6 vs atol 1e-6 (1898/6432896 elements; update 0 passed at 2.28e-7) at keep_unsharded_blocks=0/6/8 alike. That is the vocab-sharded head's fp32 GEMM-reassociation drift (shard N=25129/25128 mm vs the reference's full N=50257 mm on near-zero logits) amplified ~20x by the second update; it is inherent to the shard-local head math, not to transport or reshard policy, so the vocab-sharding route to the root unit's 2x8.2 ms collectives is dead under this project's two-update 1e-6/1e-4 gate. What survives from the same boundary is the edit those comm groups were retained for, now on its own measured basis. Current-revision evidence (execution_timeline-1221e205 + nsys-9ed9145c on fa5f081d, clean original baseline 176.20 ms rank-max, peak 2,239,245,312 B): the step is wire-bound - 74 NCCL kernels strictly serialized on the comm stream (union == sum == 163.81 ms rank 0), compute essentially hidden (compute_overlap 32.2 ms of 176.2; communication_without_compute 131.6 ms), logical payload 2.734 GB/rank: 48 block AllGathers of 25,192,448 B at ~1.99 ms (24 forward + 24 backward), 24 block ReduceScatters of 50,384,896 B at ~2.08 ms, one root AllGather and one root ReduceScatter of 105,029,632 B at ~8.2 ms, all RING/SIMPLE 2-channel over SHM/PCIe with peer access disabled (nccl_tuning-f6198e01) - so removing a collective removes ~its full duration from the critical path. Verified on the measured worker's Python (torch 2.13.0+cu129): FSDPModule.set_reshard_after_forward(False, recurse=False) is public, and FSDPParamGroup.unshard() is a no-op when is_unsharded - the exact mechanism the trace already proves in-step for the root (docstring: root default reshard_after_forward=False; only one 105 MB root AllGather exists among the 74 collectives). Keeping the K trailing (backward-first) blocks unsharded after forward therefore skips their backward re-all-gathers and nothing else: bitwise-identical trajectory (backward consumes the same all-gathered bytes the re-gather would reproduce; no update occurs between forward and backward; forward AllGathers, ReduceScatters, every GEMM shape and grad reduction are untouched - the opposite risk profile of the rejected vocab head). Memory funds the edit: cap 2,351,207,577 B (1.05x) minus baseline peak leaves 111,962,265 B ~= 2.22x a block's 50,331,648 B all-gather output; K=2 (+100.7 MB even in the worst-aligned keep window, which the source itself fills with the same blocks' backward prefetch at timeline sequences 179-180) fits unconditionally, and larger K is gated by the measured peak constraint. Boundary: the model-forward replacement installs the policy once at build (direct callable boundary, no functional replacements), the 24 FSDPGPT2Block modules are the reconfigured units, and c10d::_allgather_base_ group 04dbf05d596cce5394b5 is where the eliminated backward invocations (call c917c08825afcaacd65b752f, count 24 -> 24-K) are observed. Set-reshard-after-backward alternatives are rejected explicitly: they retain stale unsharded copies across the per-invocation optimizer update and reset, unlike the after-forward policy whose window closes at each block's post-backward reshard before any update.
